Published - November 14, 2026 01:56 am IST - MOUNT MAUNGANUI
New Zealand's Matt Henry celebrates the wicket of Shreyas Iyer during the fourth ODI cricket match between against India at the Bay Oval in Mount Maunganui on November 13, 2026. | Photo Credit: AFP
India skipper Shreyas Iyer on Friday blamed the change in the pitch for their massive 244-run defeat to New Zealand in the fourth ODI, saying it went from a belter to a seaming track.
He, however, vowed to draw inspiration from the first two ODIs, approach the next match with a fresh mind and level the series.
New Zealand posted 333 after being put in by stand-in captain Iyer, but India's batting line-up suffered a spectacular collapse, being bundled out for 89 in 26.4 overs. Pacer Matt Henry ripped through the top order to finish with figures of 6/27.
"A tough one, I guess, to take that. There was a huge difference between the wickets between innings," Iyer, who is captaining India in ODIs for the first time, said during the post-match presentation.
"But also credit where it's due, the way Henry bowled in the right areas right from ball one. I think that was sensational. We tried almost everything in the first innings, the way they were playing on the rise. And we thought that the wicket was better to bat on considering they got 330 after that. Obviously a couple of dropped catches, but that definitely happens in a game.
"But yeah, when we got into the dressing room, we thought that we would be cruising through the chase as well. But the way the ball was seaming in and out, you couldn't basically decide from inside that this is how I'm going to play. Or even if you saw the wickets, no one threw the wicket away. It was good deliveries."
The win kept New Zealand's hopes of levelling the series alive.
"It's important to forget about this one, obviously, analyze what went wrong in terms of bowling and batting. But at the back of the mind it's important that we have also won two games. So a lot of inspiration from that one and see to it that we come with a fresh set of mind," Iyer said.
New Zealand captain Mitchell Santner was pleased with his team's effort, though he felt they had initially fallen short of a competitive total by around 20 runs. The bowlers, led by Henry, made up for it by chipping away with wickets.
"Pretty happy. Didn't get to bowl again, so pretty happy. Young did his thing and we got a good score despite leaving a few out there. I think we were thinking 360, the intent was great. Maybe if we got 20 more each partnership, we could've gotten there but they chipped away with wickets," he said.
"Henry wanted to play today. With the new ball with a wicket that offers a bit, he's the best. Will chill tomorrow. Pacers will, I'll have to come and bowl. Then see what Sunday offers from a pitch and conditions point of view and take it from there."
